protocol.block: Use 4 by 4 native luminance blocks anchored at global grid multiples of four. Measure mean squared diagonal Haar coefficient on each of four disjoint 2 by 2 cells. Coarse gradient is the Euclidean norm of horizontal and vertical differences between block halves. Exclude mean luminance outside 32 to 224 and coarse gradient above 9.
protocol.conditioned: Match each mouth block to surrounding blocks within 16 luma units and 3 coarse-gradient units. Use the three nearest under normalized squared distance. Take the median of their median log detail minus mouth log detail with additive 0.5. Require eight matches and at least half the eligible mouth blocks matched.
protocol.gate: At least four strict LivePortrait locations across three groups and the strict MuseTalk location. Require 70 percent measured coverage for each strict neural family and ordinary controls, at most two ordinary flags and none on original, recompressed or hard-cut controls. Compare matched H.264 4:2:0 delivery separately.
protocol.input: Use one submitted picture stream, native RGB and pinned single-face geometry. No second file, supplied range, renderer metadata, audio or reference camera enters scoring.
protocol.plain: Compare the logarithm of the ratio of surrounding median diagonal detail to mouth median diagonal detail with additive 0.5 before dividing. Require eight blocks in each region pool.
protocol.points: The third-largest ordinary GRID development maximum per arm with a fixed floor of 0.04. Require strict exceedance. Correct localization requires native half-open temporal IoU of at least 0.50.
protocol.range: Use one verified shot, 8, 12, 16 or 20 native pictures, and five flank pictures on each side. Require 80 percent observation coverage in core and flanks. Use the smaller positive median drop against both flanks and retain one strongest interval. Before, middle and first-after pictures must have native face anchors.
protocol.regions: One mouth ellipse and three surrounding comparison ellipses on the eye-normalized plane. Only block-center coordinates are transformed. Pixel values always remain native.
